plainEnglish.title: What is the LC1D38F7 contactor?
plainEnglish.introduction: The Schneider Electric LC1D38F7 is an electrically operated switch called a contactor. A control signal energises a coil, which moves the contacts and switches the connected power circuit. This lets a control panel operate equipment without a person manually switching its power connections.
plainEnglish.example: A motor starter can use a contactor to turn a motor on when the control circuit calls for it. The contactor performs the switching; separate, correctly selected protection deals with overloads and short circuits. A contactor alone is not a complete motor starter.
plainEnglish.drawings: The 3D CAD source helps a drafter check the device's shape and position in a panel. The product's connection diagram identifies its terminals. Check the complete LC1D38F7 code, coil supply, accessories and revision: a related TeSys model may not have the same configuration. The linked family archive has not been acquired locally.

terms.name: Coil
terms.meaning: The electromagnet that operates the switch when energised.

terms.name: Contacts
terms.meaning: The conducting parts that meet or separate to close or open a circuit.

terms.name: Pole
terms.meaning: One of the separate power paths switched by the device.

plainEnglish.caption: How a contactor operates, simplified. Control and power circuits are separate; this is not a wiring diagram.

plainEnglish.title: What is the SC5000UD-MV-US-P3?
plainEnglish.introduction: The Sungrow SC5000UD-MV-US-P3 is power conversion equipment for a large battery storage installation. Batteries use direct current (DC), while the electricity grid uses alternating current (AC). A power conversion system, or PCS, provides the controlled conversion needed to move energy between them.
plainEnglish.example: When a battery installation charges, the conversion equipment helps move energy from the AC system into the DC batteries. When it discharges, energy travels back towards the AC system. The battery holds the energy; the PCS controls its conversion. They are different parts of the installation.
plainEnglish.drawings: An outline drawing helps plan the equipment's position and footprint. Electrical drawings describe its interfaces with the rest of the installation. This entry currently points to manufacturer information; editable CAD for this exact configuration has not been located or acquired. Dimensions and interfaces must come from the matching manufacturer documents.

terms.name: PCS
terms.meaning: Power conversion system: equipment used to convert and control electrical power.

terms.name: DC
terms.meaning: Direct current, the form of electricity used by the battery.

terms.name: AC
terms.meaning: Alternating current, the form used by the electricity grid.

plainEnglish.caption: Discharge direction shown. Charging reverses the flow. This explains the role of a PCS, not the product's internal construction.

plainEnglish.title: What is Leroy-Somer LSA 40?
plainEnglish.introduction: Leroy-Somer LSA 40 is a CAD resource from Nidec Leroy-Somer. Publisher CAD for an industrial alternator family, including SAE coupling and bearing/frame variants where linked. This is alternator geometry, not a complete packaged generator.
plainEnglish.example: For Leroy-Somer LSA 40, start with lsa40-8-022a.dwg. This entry lists 63 file routes in DWG, DXF. Match the filename and equipment configuration to your project, then use Nidec Leroy-Somer's drawing to check the mounting position, dimensions and connection access it actually documents.
plainEnglish.drawings: Use an outline or mounting drawing to check physical position, shape and fixing points. Use an electrical schematic to understand connections. plainEnglish.title: What is the DSE8610 MKII?
plainEnglish.introduction: The DSE8610 MKII is a controller for an engine-driven generator. Think of it as the generator's coordinator: it monitors operation, manages starting and stopping, and helps generators work together. The controller does not generate the electricity; the engine and alternator do that.
plainEnglish.example: When generators supply a site together, they must synchronise before being connected and then share the electrical load. Synchronising means matching their AC output before connection. Load sharing means dividing the work between generators. The DSE8610 MKII provides these control functions and displays operating information and alarms.
plainEnglish.drawings: The wiring CAD describes connections between the controller and other parts of the system, such as measuring devices and control circuits. It helps a drafter prepare a control-panel drawing. It is not a complete generator layout or a ready-to-build switchboard design. Use the manufacturer's drawing for the exact model and revision.

terms.name: Generator controller
terms.meaning: A device that monitors and controls a generator's operation.

terms.name: Synchronising
terms.meaning: Matching AC supplies before connecting them together.

terms.name: Load sharing
terms.meaning: Dividing electrical demand between generators operating together.

plainEnglish.caption: Information and control flow, not the power path. The controller receives measurements and sends commands to generator equipment.

plainEnglish.example: When updating a panel drawing for BTS-250 250-4P3P, insert the front DWG for the panel elevation, then compare the bottom and top views before locating the terminal connections. Retain the original filenames in the drawing register so a later revision can be matched to this set.
plainEnglish.drawings: This set uses the exact filename stem BTS-250_250-4P3P. Its views are stored in Tembreak 1/BTS. Keep these views together when coordinating the breaker outline and its terminal orientation; a different pole or connection suffix identifies a different drawing set.
checklist: Match the BTS-250 250-4P3P filename stem and all connection suffixes to the existing equipment.
Use the bottom, front, top views from this set together; do not substitute a similarly numbered frame.
Locate the drawings under Tembreak 1/BTS after extracting the original ZIP.
Treat this as a legacy drawing resource; confirm replacement equipment and accessory compatibility separately with NHP.

questions.question: Which views are provided for BTS-250 250-4P3P?
questions.answer: The original archive lists 3 matching DWG files: BTS-250_250-4P3P-Bottom.dwg, BTS-250_250-4P3P-Front.dwg, BTS-250_250-4P3P-Top.dwg. They are consolidated on this page as one drawing set.

questions.question: Is this a current-product selection guide?
questions.answer: This is the archived TemBreak 1 drawing collection. Use it to identify geometry for legacy equipment. The source product page is evidence for the collection, rather than a specification covering every filename in the archive.

questions.question: Where do I find these BTS-250 250-4P3P drawings after downloading?
questions.answer: Download the original NHP ZIP and extract it. Open the Tembreak 1/BTS folder and match the full filenames shown in the file list above.

plainEnglish.example: When updating a panel drawing for XFG-XH400NE-4P, insert the front DWG for the panel elevation, then compare the bottom views before locating the terminal connections. Retain the original filenames in the drawing register so a later revision can be matched to this set.
plainEnglish.drawings: This set uses the exact filename stem XFG-XH400NE-4P. Its views are stored in Tembreak 1/XFG Handle. Keep these views together when coordinating the breaker outline and its terminal orientation; a different pole or connection suffix identifies a different drawing set.
checklist: Match the XFG-XH400NE-4P filename stem and all connection suffixes to the existing equipment.
Use the bottom, front views from this set together; do not substitute a similarly numbered frame.
Locate the drawings under Tembreak 1/XFG Handle after extracting the original ZIP.
Treat this as a legacy drawing resource; confirm replacement equipment and accessory compatibility separately with NHP.

questions.question: Which views are provided for XFG-XH400NE-4P?
questions.answer: The original archive lists 2 matching DWG files: XFG-XH400NE-4P-Bottom.dwg, XFG-XH400NE-4P-Front.dwg. They are consolidated on this page as one drawing set.

questions.question: Is this a current-product selection guide?
questions.answer: This is the archived TemBreak 1 drawing collection. Use it to identify geometry for legacy equipment. The source product page is evidence for the collection, rather than a specification covering every filename in the archive.

questions.question: Where do I find these XFG-XH400NE-4P drawings after downloading?
questions.answer: Download the original NHP ZIP and extract it. Open the Tembreak 1/XFG Handle folder and match the full filenames shown in the file list above.

plainEnglish.example: When updating a panel drawing for XFG-XS1600NE-4P, insert the front DWG for the panel elevation, then compare the bottom views before locating the terminal connections. Retain the original filenames in the drawing register so a later revision can be matched to this set.
plainEnglish.drawings: This set uses the exact filename stem XFG-XS1600NE-4P. Its views are stored in Tembreak 1/XFG Handle. Keep these views together when coordinating the breaker outline and its terminal orientation; a different pole or connection suffix identifies a different drawing set.
checklist: Match the XFG-XS1600NE-4P filename stem and all connection suffixes to the existing equipment.
Use the bottom, front views from this set together; do not substitute a similarly numbered frame.
Locate the drawings under Tembreak 1/XFG Handle after extracting the original ZIP.
Treat this as a legacy drawing resource; confirm replacement equipment and accessory compatibility separately with NHP.

questions.question: Which views are provided for XFG-XS1600NE-4P?
questions.answer: The original archive lists 2 matching DWG files: XFG-XS1600NE-4P-Bottom.dwg, XFG-XS1600NE-4P-Front.dwg. They are consolidated on this page as one drawing set.

questions.question: Is this a current-product selection guide?
questions.answer: This is the archived TemBreak 1 drawing collection. Use it to identify geometry for legacy equipment. The source product page is evidence for the collection, rather than a specification covering every filename in the archive.

questions.question: Where do I find these XFG-XS1600NE-4P drawings after downloading?
questions.answer: Download the original NHP ZIP and extract it. Open the Tembreak 1/XFG Handle folder and match the full filenames shown in the file list above.
